title: Module 7 Interpretation Check
intro: Each item gives you a short research situation. Decide what the evidence supports.

items.q: A sample of 10 has M = 55 and s = 8. The hypothesized mean is 50. What is the estimated standard error?
items.why: sM = 8 divided by the square root of 10 = 2.53.

items.q: Using that estimated standard error, what is t?
With df = 9 and alpha = .05 two-tailed, the critical t is 2.262. What is the decision?
o: Retain the null, because 1.98 is below 2.262
Reject the null, because t is positive
Reject the null, because the mean difference is 5
items.why: The obtained t falls outside the critical region. The exact p value is about .08.

items.q: Cohen's d for this sample is the mean difference divided by s. What is d?
items.why: d = 5/8 = .625. The effect is medium in size even though the test is not significant, which is a sign of low power with only 10 people.

items.q: The 95 percent CI for the population mean is 55 plus or minus 2.262(2.53). What are the limits?
items.why: 2.262 times 2.53 is 5.72. The CI runs from 49.28 to 60.72 and includes 50, matching the nonsignificant test.
